deal_stage: Technical assessment in progress, committee presentation expected next quarter
pitch_summary: Multi-agent Gen AI platform to automate tax and logistics reconciliation between Magalog and more than 90 external carrier clients, eliminating the manual bottleneck of NF-e/CT-e (Brazilian tax and freight document) reconciliation that today limits the scaling of the logistics-as-a-service operation.
proposed_solution: Agentic pipeline on Azure with tax-document reading, freight reconciliation, and exception-handling agents under human supervision, integrated with 175 cross-docking hubs and 21 distribution centers. 20-week implementation, US$580k in Year 1 (license + services).

ceo: Frederico Trajano has been CEO of Magalu since 2016, having started his career at the company in the early 2000s helping build out its e-commerce
Created Luizalabs, the company's technology lab, today a benchmark for digitalization in Brazilian retail
In recent public communications, positions the company as a leader of the 'ia-commerce revolution,' the natural successor to e-commerce and mobile-commerce

Under his leadership, Magalu posted R$65 billion in total sales in 2024 (72% via e-commerce), with 1,245 physical stores, 21 distribution centers, and 175 cross-docking hubs, serving 37 million customers across 917 cities
The logistics-as-a-service unit, Magalog, grew 47% in revenue in 2025 and now serves more than 90 market clients unrelated to the Magalu ecosystem, in addition to operating the group's own brands
Trajano turned a negative net cash position of R$0.5 billion into a positive balance of R$3.1 billion, pairing growth with financial discipline, and completed a decade leading the company in 2025

Given this track record of expansion via a proprietary technology ecosystem (Luizalabs, Magalog, Magalu Cloud, Magalu Ads), he tends to evaluate automation proposals through the lens of 'does this accelerate Magalog's scale as a third-party logistics platform, or is it just incremental internal efficiency?'
